This week is defined by two parts. I went on a trip this weekend where I ate and drank whatever I wanted for 3 days and walked numerous miles throughout the day. My average daily caloric intake during the week was 882 cal. I met my goal of consuming 800 - 1000 cal a day except for 2 days which had an intake of 559 and 1155. 1155 was Thursday when I traveled for the trip so I drank a little that night when I made it to the destination. My estimated average daily caloric intake for the weekend(WE) was 3200. We ate out every meal and had numerous drinks each night.

I did fairly well during the week in preparation for this trip. My mid week weigh-in came in at 183.5 lbs., meeting the goal that I had. According to my logging site, I've used 5981 more cal than I ate. Despite my overconsumption on the WE, I still walked around a lot and used up plenty of calories. Not enough to be a deficit for the day, but my calorie deficit during the week was at least 1000 each of those days. This should translate to 1.7 lbs. of real weight lose. I appear to have broke even but I expect to have a higher weight lose next week due to my overeating and drinking the night before a weigh-in.

I went for a run four times this week. I did a 5k for one of those runs. My shortest run was about 1.5 miles.

Failures:

* Snacked on the road. Could have saved 700 calories for the week.

I am honestly content with the fact that getting drunk two nights and eating everything I wanted three days did not make me gain weight for the week. I have noticed that I don't eat the volume that I used to and that helped me not get too many calories. I hope my stomach shrinks a little bit more.

I've decided to start weightlifting next week. I would like to lose a little bit more fat and get a better weight baseline. I need to spend time this week researching techniques and forms and make sure that I pick something good for me. I plan to hop back onto my strict diet this week and keep most days below 1000 calories. There is a game night on Friday so I might slip up there and then there is a Super Bowl party I'll be going to so I will probably not be below 1000 calories those days. I do plan to not go over 2000 calories on those days.

My casual shirts are beginning to look terrible on me too now and one of my belts is now retired since the last loop on it is still too big.

Regarding working out, a very good program to start with is called Stronglifts5x5. You can read about it here: http://stronglifts.com/5x5/

If you've never worked out before, this is an excellent place to start. It's not complicated, there are only 5 exercises total, and only 3 per day. It starts out so light you can barely tell you're doing anything, but it gets you inside a gym 3x per week. The first month is all about the mental part of being inside the gym, the second month you realize you're working out, and the third month you're reaching your max and possibly lifting more than most people inside the gym.

Doubtful you'll make it much past 3 months, but at that point you know how strong you are, you know you can keep a routine, and you can re-evaluate and do something that you want to do next with the exact information required to do so.

As a relatively happy GOG patron, this concession towards "early access" (however more sane and... controlled? than Steam's approach) causes me some degree of consternation.
I posted this news last week and also expressed my dislike of it. Of course, the CoD fangirls went crazy with the downvotes.

I mean... you could just not buy those games. The difference between this and Kickstarter, is that with Kickstarter you're donating some money to someone and hopefully you'll get what you were expecting way down the line. Early access allows you to buy a game in development and then get your money back (within 14 days) if you don't feel like it's worth it.

Personally I'm more apt to buy something on early access than Kickstarter.

I mean... you could just not buy those games.

Yes, this is true. On a related note, I would strongly recommend that anyone who has not already bought into Starbound stay as far away from it as humanly possible. Do NOT give Chucklefish your money - they're an absolutely terrible company, their game has been in "early access" since motherfucking 2012, and it's likely never going to actually be finished. (I bought it when it was on Steam - I regret that to this day)

The difference between this and Kickstarter, is that with Kickstarter you're donating some money to someone and hopefully you'll get what you were expecting way down the line.

While you get more (potentially) from early access than you do from being a Kickstarter backer (usually, really depends on what backer rewards are laid out in the KS), it's still not a very good deal. KS/crowdfunding has plenty of its own peccadilloes, to be sure (just ask any poor fool who backed Mighty Number 9, Ant Simulator, etc.)

Early access allows you to buy a game in development and then get your money back (within 14 days) if you don't feel like it's worth it.

This IS an important distinction to make, yes (at least in the case of GOG's early access system). GOG has made a very consumer-friendly choice by enabling users to get returns on what they feel are bad investments, and I do appreciate that. (I don't think Steam refunds were in place yet when I bought into Starbound, lord I wish they had been)

Personally I'm more apt to buy something on early access than Kickstarter.

That is your money, your time and your decision, and more power to you. Just keep a very sharp eye on your investments.
